doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Meeting Louis Armstrong at the New Orleans airport as a child
summary: Around 1963 Brunious's father took him to the airport where a brass band greeted Armstrong, who rubbed his head.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That’s got to be like the best dream you could have I think. When I was a little kid, it was about 1963 or something like that, Louis Armstrong came to New Orleans. And this big brass band like George Lewis and Punch Miller and my dad and everybody went out there to meet Louis. And my dad told my brother and I said, “Look, get some clothes on, I’m going to take you someplace” you know and we were wondering where we were going. He said, “I’m going to take you see Louis Armstrong.” I really didn’t think I would see Louis Armstrong. But we went to the airport and when Louis stepped out of the plane, man that band hit — boom. And a smile came over Louis Armstrong’s face. He had a white baseball cap on and it was just something I could never forget. And he rubbed me on the head like that. “Hey Pops.” That was one of the greatest moments of my life.
I mean we keep saying this enough about Louis Armstrong, but we keep going.
Well if anything, I hope all this talk, whoever might see this, if they haven’t examined those records, and it doesn’t matter, it doesn’t matter what record, if he’s on it, it’s going to be great.
It doesn’t matter whether it’s the 20s or the 30s or 40s or 50s or 60s.
